findings.failure_path: default_branch, current_branch and origin_flag used to be set from the hook cwd before the segment loop. Now they are filled only inside the git push|merge|pull branch. Any other consumer, such as is_default_branch for gh pr merge or HTTP merge-API segments, or the current branch used by a gh merge with no PR number, now sees empty values. For a repo whose default branch is e.g. 'release', it falls back to main/master/dev/develop/trunk, so a merge that was denied before can now be allowed. The test only counts git spawns for non-landing commands and does not cover gh/HTTP merges against a non-standard default branch.
findings.smallest_fix: Call ensure_base_git_context, then copy the base_* values into default_branch/current_branch/origin_flag, in every gh/HTTP merge branch that reads them. Add a test: a repo with origin/HEAD=release, run 'gh pr merge' / the HTTP merge form, and expect deny.

findings.failure_path: The boundary set [\s;&|<>()/] has no backtick. In a command like echo `rm skills/x/SKILL.md`, 'rm' follows a backtick, so the regex does not match. There is no > or \ either, so may_write_from_bash returns False and the shared-skill checkpoint is skipped, if host-input treats command substitution as a write.
findings.smallest_fix: Add ` (and {, !) to the leading boundary class and add a backtick write case to test_non_write_bash_and_unhandled_events_do_not_load_normalizer.

findings.failure_path: The fast path allows any payload whose raw text lacks the case-sensitive substrings Edit/Write/apply_patch. If a host bridge sends lowercase tool names (e.g. OpenCode/Antigravity 'edit'/'write') to the engine without a $1 override, an edit to a path in an opted-in repo outside $PWD is allowed with no jq parse. The diff has no evidence that every caller uses canonical casing.
findings.smallest_fix: Match case-insensitively (shopt -s nocasematch around the case statement, or add *edit*|*write*|*patch*). Alternatively, add a test showing that every bridge passes canonical tool names or $1.

concern_results.conclusion: Most fast paths look sound on the paths I traced. Two open gaps: the merge guard's base context now loads only for git push/merge/pull, and the Bash write prefilter ignores backticks.

There is a possible permission-guard narrowing. Before this change the hook-cwd default/current branch was always set. It is now unset for any segment that is not git push/merge/pull, and the diff does not show that no other consumer needs it.

Fail-closed handling still holds for unreadable roots and files: Ruby exits 2 and the shell maps that to exit 1. The validate-skill pre-check also fails closed, and the stamp cache falls back to an uncached run. The cat-file batch raises on EOF or a short read, which produces a partial.

The tests count spawns and spot-check a few write shapes. No test shows that may_write_from_bash covers everything host-input.bash_write_targets can return, or that gh/HTTP merge paths still see the resolved default branch for a repo whose default isn't main/master.

Bindings parity is kept, and the OpenCode Stop path is unchanged. The nested-export downgrade in check-size-budget is a deliberate narrowing and is documented. I found no scope creep beyond the request.
Reversible with git revert. CCL_SKILL_NO_SELFTEST_CACHE gives a runtime bypass, and the Makefile keeps an uncached self-test.
Gate tokens are preserved. validate-skill's scan-error message no longer names the failing root on rg errors. That is minor.
The 'conservative over-approximation of host-input.bash_write_targets' claim is asserted, not shown. The backtick case below is a counterexample.
The merge-guard lazy-loading boundary needs proof that every reader of default_branch/current_branch/origin_flag calls ensure_base_git_context first.
hooks/AGENTS.md was updated to match the new jq and Stop behavior, and the scripts AGENTS.md lists the new test. I found no contract violations.
